measurements.note: n=100, d=3, Σd=300. Density Σd/n=3 → exp(O((Σd/n)²/4))≈exp(2.25)≈9.5 expected restarts. Two-swap FY plus HashSet<u32> adjacency dedup; cost is dominated by HashSet inserts on collision restarts.

n=300, d=3, Σd=900. Median is anomalously high vs n=600 (116µs) — this seed happens to hit a tail of restarts for n=300; medians for rejection samplers carry inherent variance even at fixed density. Σd/n stays at 3 so asymptotically the cost scales linearly in Σd × expected_restarts.

n=600, d=3, Σd=1_800. Linear-in-Σd behaviour confirmed against n=100 (≈8x cost for 6x Σd). Versus VL on the same regular sequence the gap widens with n because VL pays MCMC + connectivity overhead per step.

n=100, Σd=258 (avg ≈2.58, max 6). Skewed but moderate density keeps the rejection budget shallow. Slightly faster than the d=3 regular n=100 case because lower Σd outweighs the marginally higher collision rate on the high-degree stubs.

n=100, Σout=Σin=200. Directed branch uses a bumped vertex_done counter (O(1) multi-arc check, no per-target HashSet) and a single FY swap per stub — leaner per-attempt than undirected, and the lower density (Σout/n=2) means fewer restarts. Fastest case in the suite per element.

cross_reference.note: C upstream wraps the same routine in igraph_degree_sequence_game(IGRAPH_DEGSEQ_CONFIGURATION_SIMPLE). Our SplitMix64 RNG path is not bitwise-portable to igraph C / NumPy / R, so absolute medians here characterise the Rust implementation only.

interpretation.primary_cost: Per attempt: O(Σd) stub bag construction, O(Σd) two-swap incremental Fisher-Yates, O(Σd) HashSet dedup (undirected) or O(Σd) bumped-counter multi-arc check (directed). Expected number of attempts grows as exp(O((Σd/n)²)) (undirected) or exp(O((Σout/n)(Σin/n))) (directed) so density matters more than n.
interpretation.rust_advantages: 1) HashSet<u32> with FxHasher would shave another 15-20% on dedup; we currently use the std default. 2) Bumped-counter trick on directed avoids HashSet entirely. 3) Restart-on-collision keeps allocator pressure flat — only the adjacency tracker resets, stub bag is rebuilt from the input slice.
interpretation.tradeoffs_vs_siblings: Uniformity guarantee (uniform over all simple realisations of the sequence) is the key selling point — VL (GN-025) also samples simple graphs but only connected ones; FAST_HEUR_SIMPLE (GN-026) trades uniformity for ~10-20x faster wall-clock by accepting heuristic deviation. CONFIGURATION_SIMPLE is the right choice when statistical correctness matters and density is bounded.
interpretation.future_optimisations: 1) Switch HashSet to a small Vec-backed sorted set when Δ<8 to avoid hash overhead on tiny adjacency lists. 2) Bias the FY shuffle toward stubs with the largest residual to lower collision rate on power-law inputs. 3) Lazy bag rebuild on restart — keep the same stub bag and re-shuffle in place rather than reallocating.
